history.period: Late 11th century (c. 1060-1070, per art historian Adam Hardy); inscriptional evidence of Hoysala additions up to 1131 CE
history.summary: CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected: the temple is at Balligavi (ancient inscriptions: Belagami/Belligave/Ballagamve/Ballipura), near Shikaripura, Shivamogga district. Balligavi was an important 11th-12th century city under Western Chalukya rule, described in inscriptions as 'Anadi Rajadhani' (ancient capital) and dotted with agrahara learning centres. The Kedareshvara is a trikuta (three-shrine) temple in a transitional Western Chalukya-Hoysala style, built in soapstone: the central and south shrines hold Shivalingas (the south one identified as Brahma), and the north shrine holds an image of Janardhana (Vishnu) - symbolising the Hindu trinity. Two Hoysala emblems were added in 1060 CE. NOTE: some sources claim the western shrine dates to the 7th-8th century and others credit construction to Hoysala King Veera Ballala II - these conflict with the standard dating (CONFLICT - verify). Protected as a monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India. Coordinates are geocoder-level approximations.

name: Kedareshvara Temple, Balligavi
town_description: Balligavi (also Belagami/Belligave in medieval inscriptions) is a historic town in Shikaripura taluk of Shivamogga district, Karnataka. A major centre of religion, education and commerce under the 11th-12th century Western Chalukyas - called the 'City of Temples' and described in inscriptions as an ancient capital - it is mentioned in over 80 inscriptions. Today it is a quiet village known for its Kedareshvara and Tripurantakesvara temples and its agrahara (Brahmin learning centre) heritage.
